text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG

- Heads of the ruling coalition parties and heads of their parliamentary parties meet in Bonn to discuss how to push forward tax reform proposals. Likely to discuss offer by Finance Minister Theo Waigel to talk with opposition Social Democrats (SPD) about the reforms.
- In a contribution to the newspaper British writer Salman Rushdie attacks European policies and calls for "new determination in the fight against the god of thunder that is Iran."
- The economics ministers of the east German states defend the high level of aid they receive, rejecting suggestions that it should be drastically cut.

- Health Minister Horst Seehofer says hospital patients will probably not have to pay higher additional costs on top of their insurance. Patients in west Germany currently pay 25 marks per day in hospital, those in the east pay 20 marks.
- Record run on the Frankfurt bourse continues, with the DAX index of 30 leading shares reaching a record high for the tenth day in a row of 3,229.48 points.
HANDELSBLATT

- SPD parliamentary leader Rudolf Scharping says party to invite the government to talks over tax reform this month. The SDP maintains it wants the reforms to take effect by the beginning of next year.
- Allianz Lebensversicherung AG, the life insurance unit of Allianz AG Holding, says group premium income rose by 3.8 percent to 12 billion marks.
- Insurance group Colonia Konzern AG calculates the costs of a potential change in the pension insurance law.
- Brewing and drinks group Brau und Brunnen sacks group head Friedrich Ebeling.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Bavarian state premier Edmund Stoiber wants proposed tax reforms to be agreed quickly -- by April at the latest.
- Fewer jobs that thought -- around 120,000 -- are dependent on the German coal industry, say coal companies and IG Bergbau.
- Foreigners have a right to reclaim property taken by the former East German state, while German citizens do not.
- German DAX share index reaches record high.
DIE WELT
- Finance Minister Waigel and SPD on track for discussions over government's planned tax reform.
- Federal constitutional court orders two judges to pay fines for misusing the court.

- Although the CDU and SPD in Mecklenbug-Vorpommern seemed to have reached agreement on the planned route of the high-speed Transrapid raliway between Hamburg and Berlin, the SPD are now maintaining a critical distance to the project.
-- Bonn Newsroom +49 228 26097160
